content: The user's overall instructions for the dataset analysis are: Investigate potential periods of digester instability. The digesters each have a volume of 1625m3. TWAS and PS loads are evenly split. HSW is split as shown in the data.. Here is the information for summary: Data description: Excel workbook containing (1) daily time-series operating and monitoring data for two anaerobic digesters and associated feed streams at the Muscatine WRRF during calendar year 2022, and (2) a data dictionary defining each field, units, and acceptable values. Sheet name: daily_data Headings: Year, Month, Day, V-TWAS_m3d, V-PS_m3d, V-HSW_m3d, HSW-Dig1-portion_pct, HSW2-Dig2-portion_pct, Dig1-T_degC, Dig2-T_degC, Dig1-pH, Dig2-pH, FOG_m3d, HSW-VS_percent, HSW-COD_mgL, Dig1-alk_mgL, Dig2-alk_mgL, Dig1-VFA_mgL, Dig2-VFA_mgL, Dig1-VFA-Alkalinity_ratio, Dig2-VFA-Alkalinity_ratio, Q-influent_m3d, BOD-influent_mgL, TWAS-VS_percent, PS-VS_percent, Biogas_m3d Time period: 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31 Time step: 1 day Time format: Date components stored as separate integer columns: Year, Month, Day (YYYY, M, D) Sheet name: dictionary Headings: Element or value display name, Description, Unit, Data type, Acceptable values Time period: Not applicable to Not applicable Time step: Not applicable Time format: Not applicable ####Chart: Digester VFA to Alkalinity Ratio Time Series (Dig 1 vs Dig 2) Digester 1 shows the clearest instability signal in late Sep–mid Oct. The VFA/Alk ratio rises above the 0.40 upset line repeatedly from ~2022-09-21 through 2022-10-20, peaking at ~0.93 on 2022-09-30 (also ~0.74 on 2022-09-29 and ~0.67 on 2022-10-13). This pattern is consistent with acid accumulation outpacing buffering and suggests a sustained loading/feeding or mixing/heating issue rather than a single-day lab anomaly. Digester 2 is generally stable (mostly 0.12–0.22) but has short spikes above 0.40 in late Jan–early Feb (max ~0.52 on 2022-01-26) and again around early Oct (~0.45 on 2022-10-07), indicating brief stress events. Use the CSV to flag days >0.30 (caution) and >0.40 (upset) and correlate to feed splits and HSW/FOG events next. Chart image: . ####Chart: Digester pH Time Series (Dig 1 vs Dig 2) pH is generally within the 6.8–7.2 band for much of the year, but there is a pronounced divergence during the Digester 1 VFA/Alk upset window identified earlier. Key instability indicators: - Digester 1 pH drops below 6.8 repeatedly from ~2022-09-28 through ~2022-10-20, reaching a minimum of ~6.43 on 2022-10-20 (also ~6.50 on 2022-09-30 and 2022-10-13). This aligns with the late-Sep VFA/Alk spike and supports a true souring episode rather than noise. - Digester 2 remains mostly near-neutral during the same period, but hits a minimum of ~6.49 on 2022-10-13 and shows a low outlier ~6.74 on 2022-05-04. The Nov–Dec period trends slightly lower (often ~6.9–7.1), consistent with reduced alkalinity reserve or higher acid formation; check alkalinity trends next. Chart image: . ####Chart: Digester Alkalinity Time Series (Dig 1 vs Dig 2) Alkalinity provides strong corroboration of the late-Sep/Oct Digester 1 instability. Digester 1 alkalinity trends downward through Sep and then collapses below the 3000 mg/L line multiple times from ~2022-09-24 through ~2022-10-21, reaching ~1965 mg/L on 2022-10-20 (also ~2078 mg/L on 2022-10-13 and ~2555 mg/L on 2022-09-30). This loss of buffering explains the concurrent low pH and high VFA/Alk. Digester 2 alkalinity is generally higher during that same window (often ~4,000–5,700 mg/L), suggesting the upset was localized to Digester 1 rather than plantwide. However, Digester 2 shows an unusual sharp dip in late May (down to ~2222 mg/L on 2022-05-25 and ~2276 mg/L on 2022-05-27) while Digester 1 also dips (~2935–3167 mg/L). That late-May event looks like a shared disturbance (sampling, dilution, or feed change) worth cross-checking against HSW/FOG volumes and splits. Late Nov–Dec both digesters drift toward ~2,700–3,400 mg/L, reducing buffer margin going into winter. Chart image: . ####Chart: Calculated Hydraulic Retention Time (HRT) by Digester Calculated HRT shows several periods where feed distribution (primarily HSW split) likely differed materially between digesters, creating asymmetric loading that can drive localized instability. Notable features: - Early year (Jan–mid Jun) HRTs are mostly identical and typically ~15–35 d, consistent with assumed 50/50 HSW split (portion data largely missing then). - From early Jul through Sep, Digester 1 frequently runs below the 15 d reference (often ~9–14 d), while Digester 2 is elevated (commonly ~30–55 d). This implies Digester 1 was receiving a much larger share of total feed (especially HSW), increasing acidification risk. - The late-Sep/Oct instability window for Digester 1 (high VFA/Alk, low pH, low alkalinity) coincides with sustained low HRT in Sep (many days ~9–13 d) followed by swings in early Oct. - Extreme HRT spikes (~100+ d on 2022-10-25 and 2022-11-06) indicate near-zero calculated feed on those dates (likely missing/zero volumes), so treat those as data-quality flags rather than true process conditions. Next: overlay the HSW split % and HSW volume on the upset window to confirm the load shift. Chart image: . ####Chart: 7-Day Rolling Average VS Loading Rate (Dig 1 vs Dig 2) The 7‑day average VS OLR highlights a pronounced mid‑year load transfer to Digester 1 that aligns with the subsequent Digester 1 stability loss. Observations tied to instability: - Jan–Jun: both digesters track closely, typically ~1.5–2.6 kgVS/m³-d. - Jul–Sep: Digester 1 ramps sharply while Digester 2 drops. Digester 1 exceeds the 3.2 kgVS/m³-d “upper typical” line for extended periods (late Jul/early Aug peaks ~3.7–3.8; late Sep peaks ~4.6 on ~2022-09-29). During the same time, Digester 2 is suppressed (~0.5–1.0), consistent with HSW being preferentially routed to Digester 1. - The highest Digester 1 OLR period (roughly 2022-09-20 to 2022-10-02, ~3.9–4.6) precedes/overlaps the maximum VFA/Alk and minimum pH/alkalinity window, supporting overloading as a primary driver. - Early Oct shows an abrupt crossover: Digester 1 OLR collapses to ~0.46 while Digester 2 spikes to ~3.0 (around 2022-10-06 to 2022-10-09). This kind of rapid redistribution can further destabilize (washout/feeding shock). Recommendation: use the CSV to compute cumulative days above 3.2 for each digester and compare to VFA/Alk excursions. Chart image: . ####Chart: High Strength Waste (HSW) Split Proportion by Digester HSW routing is highly non-uniform in mid/late 2022 and explains the asymmetric VS OLR/HRT patterns. Key periods: - Jan–mid Apr: effectively 50/50 (likely because split data missing and default assumption applied). - 2022-04-20 to 2022-04-24: abrupt swings, including 100% to Digester 1 on 2022-04-21 and 100% to Digester 2 on 2022-04-22 to 2022-04-24. These are strong step changes that can shock each digester. - 2022-07-08 through 2022-09-29: prolonged period of ~100% HSW to Digester 1 (with a few brief exceptions around early Aug). This aligns with (1) Digester 1 low HRT / high 7‑day VS OLR and (2) the late-Sep/Oct Digester 1 souring indicators (high VFA/Alk, low pH, low alkalinity). - 2022-10-01 through 2022-10-10: flip to ~100% HSW to Digester 2, matching the abrupt OLR crossover seen in early Oct. - Late Oct–Dec: returns near ~50/50 with small day-to-day noise. This chart strongly supports “feed split management” as the primary lever behind the observed instability periods. Chart image: . ####Chart: Daily Biogas Production Time Series Biogas production is highly variable (roughly ~1,200–9,350 m³/d) around the 2022 mean of ~4,716 m³/d. Signals that may align with instability / operational changes: - A sustained higher-than-average biogas period occurs from ~2022-09-20 through ~2022-10-07 (often ~5,600–7,700 m³/d), coincident with the Digester 1 high VS OLR period and the onset of the Digester 1 VFA/Alk increase. This can occur when high-strength feed boosts gas temporarily, even as buffering erodes. - The deepest single-day drop is 2022-11-06 at ~155 m³/d, which is far below surrounding values and is likely an instrumentation/outage or data error rather than true biology. - Late Dec shows repeated peaks (up to ~9,350 m³/d on 2022-12-29), suggesting high feed strength/volume or improved conversion; however, alkalinity in late year is relatively low (~2,700–3,400 mg/L), so this higher gas period may still be operating with reduced buffer. To better link gas to stability, the next useful metric is “biogas per kg VS added” (specific gas yield) using the same VS load calculations used for OLR. Chart image: . ####Chart: Digester Temperature Time Series (Dig 1 vs Dig 2) Temperature control appears generally stable in the mesophilic band and is unlikely to be the primary driver of the late-Sep/Oct Digester 1 souring. Key points: - For most of 2022 both digesters operate tightly around ~35.4–35.8 °C, well within the 34–36 °C reference band. - There are a few short, notable Digester 1 low outliers: ~33.33–33.44 °C around 2022-03-11 to 2022-03-12, and two extreme one-day drops to ~31.11 °C on 2022-08-04 and ~31.28 °C on 2022-08-31. Those are severe if real; they could also be sensor glitches given the immediate return to normal. - The main Digester 1 instability period (late Sep–mid Oct) occurs with temperature steady near ~35.4–35.7 °C, suggesting the upset was driven by organic overloading / HSW routing and loss of alkalinity rather than heating failure. If those August low temperature points are real, check for heater/recirc outages; even brief cold shocks can reduce methanogenesis and contribute to VFA buildup when loading remains high. Chart image: . ####Table: Digester Instability Event Chronology (Threshold-Based) Threshold-based event detection highlights Digester 1 as the primary instability locus, with the dominant event 2022-09-20 to 2022-10-03 (14 d). That event includes: max VFA/Alk 0.930, 8 days >0.40, min pH 6.50 (4 days <6.8), min alkalinity 2555 mg/L (3 days <3000), max 7d VS OLR 4.574 (14 days >3.2), and 10 days with ≥90% of HSW routed to Digester 1. Secondary Digester 1 events include: - 2022-07-20 to 2022-07-24 (5 d) and 2022-08-09 to 2022-08-10 (2 d): high OLR coincident with HSW mostly to Dig 1 (preconditioning for later upset). - 2022-10-13 to 2022-10-15 and 2022-10-19 to 2022-10-21: follow-on upset signatures (VFA/Alk + low alkalinity, intermittent low pH). Digester 2 events are shorter and mostly “VFA/Alk upset” spikes early year; late-year (2022-12-02 to 2022-12-16) is dominated by low alkalinity (13 d <3000) with some low pH. Use this CSV as the working chronology to align operational logs (HSW receiving, mixing/heating, antifoam/alkalinity addition, feed equalization). content:
### Summary of findings

#### Key Observations & Process Performance
Data analysis reveals a severe, sustained process instability event localized to Digester 1 during late September through October 2022. Key upset indicators in Digester 1 included:
* **VFA/Alkalinity Ratio:** Exceeded the 0.40 instability threshold repeatedly, peaking at 0.93 on September 30.
* **pH & Buffering Capacity:** pH dropped below 6.8 (reaching a low of 6.43 on October 20), coinciding with an alkalinity collapse below 2,000 mg/L (as $\text{CaCO}_3$).
* **Loading & Retention:** 7-day average Volatile Solids Organic Loading Rate (VS OLR) spiked to 4.57 $\text{kg VS/m}^3\cdot\text{d}$ (exceeding the 3.2 threshold), while Hydraulic Retention Time (HRT) dropped below 10 days.

Digester 2 remained generally stable throughout the year, though it experienced brief VFA spikes in early spring and reduced buffering capacity in December.

#### Root Cause Analysis & Interconnections
Cross-chart synthesis confirms that asymmetric High-Strength Waste (HSW) routing was the primary root cause. Between July and late September, nearly 100% of the HSW load was continuously directed to Digester 1. This unmanaged organic shock load drove acidogenesis beyond methanogenic capacity, rapidly consuming alkalinity buffer and causing digester souring.

#### Proposed Solutions
* **Automated Feed Equalization:** Implement strict feed-splitting logic to distribute HSW loads evenly between digesters based on active capacity and target OLRs.
* **Feed Throttling Controls:** Interlock HSW feeding to automatically reduce or halt intake if HRT falls below 15 days or OLR exceeds 3.2 $\text{kg VS/m}^3\cdot\text{d}$.
* **Buffer Supplementation:** Initiate automated chemical dosing (e.g., sodium bicarbonate or lime) when VFA/Alk ratios cross the 0.30 caution threshold.

#### Further Analyses & Investigations
* **Advanced Data Modeling:** Compute specific biogas yield ($\text{m}^3/\text{kg VS}$ added/destroyed) and calculate Volatile Solids Reduction (VSR) efficiency across both units.
* **Waste Characterization & Profiling:** Perform routine bench testing of HSW deliveries to evaluate composition, VFA speciation, lipid content, and potential toxicity/inhibition.
* **Field Diagnostics:** Conduct mixing energy evaluations and tracer testing to rule out dead zones, short-circuiting, or thermal stratification inside the reactors.
